evidence.claim_anchor: Weber is generally regarded, alongside Karl Marx and Emile Durkheim, as one of the three principal architects of modern sociology; his interpretive sociological method and his comparative studies of religion, capitalism, and bureaucracy shaped the discipline fundamentally.

edges.note: Co-founding 4-cluster for field:sociology: Comte (wave3 A5, coined the term) + Durkheim (wave3 A6, institutionalized) + Weber (wave3 A7, interpretive approach) + Marx (A1, conflict theory / historical materialism). Marx is typically framed alongside Weber and Durkheim as a 'three principal architects' cluster (per Britannica's Weber entry, which explicitly names Marx). edges.rationale: Britannica's formulation of the founding cluster for sociology explicitly names Marx alongside Weber and Durkheim; his historical-materialism / conflict-theory strand is treated as co-foundational in standard sociology curriculum.
